about: The wind the aircraft measured itself (spec: Weather and wind, 'The aircraft'; analyzers/wind.py). Steady windows of the primary estimator core: window_s long, with at least min_samples rows, at least min_height_m above take-off, horizontal acceleration under max_accel m/s/s, climb or descent under max_climb m/s, tilt under max_tilt_deg. Per body axis, drag = -k1 v - k2 v|v| + b (v the airspeed, b the lean needed in still air), fitted with the wind over the flight's windows: the linear model by least squares, then Gauss-Newton (iterations at most, k2 starting at k2_start), the quadratic kept when it lowers the Bayesian information criterion. A flight is measured only with min_windows windows whose ground speeds span min_speed_span m/s (10th to 90th percentile), and only when the bootstrap interval of its wind speed (resamples, seed, level) is narrower than max_interval_ms. The peak is the peak_percentile percentile of the windows' wind speeds. Uncalibrated against real aircraft: checked in ArduPilot's simulator.
sources: the drag model: a rotor moving edgewise through the air is pushed back in proportion to the airspeed (rotor momentum drag, H-force), so a multirotor's forward and sideways specific force in steady flight is drag, which the accelerometers alone sense (Mahony, Kumar and Corke, Multirotor Aerial Vehicles: Modeling, Estimation, and Control of Quadrotor, IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine 19(3), 2012, sections on rotor drag); the frame adds bluff-body drag in the square of the airspeed (Leishman, Principles of Helicopter Aerodynamics, 2nd ed., 2006, ch. 5)

ArduPilot uses the same two terms: EKF3 drag fusion (EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X/Y for the bluff body, EK3_DRAG_MCOEF for momentum drag; libraries/AP_NavEKF3 at Copter-4.7.0) and the simulator's frame model (libraries/SITL/SIM_Frame.cpp: areaCd from refSpd and refAngle, and mdrag_coef per motor in SIM_Motor.cpp)

min_speed_span and the bootstrap: the drag and the wind are told apart only by flying at different airspeeds and headings; in ArduPilot's simulator a flight of legs at 3, 6 and 9 m/s on eight headings measured a set wind within a few percent, while a hover alone could not (tests/test_wind_fixture.py)

the estimator's own wind is read from XKF2 VWN and VWE only when drag fusion runs (rules/no_gnss.json, readiness drag: EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X or _Y above 1, or EK3_DRAG_MCOEF above 0.001); otherwise EKF3 keeps its wind states at zero

calibration: the drag moves with the mass (it is an acceleration) and with the frame, so it is borrowed only within a payload band and a build; in ArduPilot's simulator a hover-only flight read the set 5 m/s from 270 degrees as 5.01 m/s from 271 with the drag of a calm flight of the same airframe (tests/test_wind_measured.py)

calibration.about: A flight that cannot measure its own drag (a hover, one speed) borrows its airframe's: the median of the fitted drag and lean in still air of the latest flights (at most flights) in the same payload band and on the same build, with a measured wind of their own; it needs min_windows steady windows (weather/measured.py). The square term is used when most of those flights fitted it.
